Apple Silicon & Intel · macOS 13+ · native Swift

Two panels, one workspace. Select a file in the left panel, press ⌥⌘→, it lands in the right. No dragging, no new windows.

Why it's different

Every action has a key.

Chorded gestures for power, plus Finder's own conventions for copy, paste, go-to-folder and Quick Look — so your muscle memory just transfers.

Undo anything.

Every move, copy, rename and trash is reversible. Multi-level ⌘Z, with a toast that says exactly what was undone.

Real Finder tags.

Genuine Apple Finder tags that round-trip both ways. Diptychon rides the ecosystem instead of inventing its own.

Every command, one place

Panels & navigation
Switch active panelTab
Open folder / fileReturn
Go up⌘↑
Back · Forward⌘[ · ⌘]
Go to folder⌘⇧G
Type-ahead filter⌘F
Show hidden files⌘⇧.
Show sidebar⌘B
File operations
Copy · Paste⌘C · ⌘V
Paste as move⌥⌘V
Duplicate · Rename⌘D · ⌘R
New folder · New file⌘⇧N · ⌃⌘N
Move to Trash⌘⌫
Undo · Redo⌘Z · ⇧⌘Z
Undo is multi-level across move, copy, trash and rename. Overwrites are the exception — Diptychon says so instead of faking an undo.
Across panels
Copy to other panel⌥⌘→ · ⌥⌘←
Move to other panel⌥⇧⌘→ · ⌥⇧⌘←
The active panel is the source, the inactive one is the destination — the arrow is simply which side is inactive.
Selection
Select all⌘A
Clear selectionEsc
Invert selection⌘⇧I
Tags & staging
Edit Finder tags⌘T
Add to Staging⌘⇧S
Show Staging panel⌘⇧B
Remove from Staging⌫
View & tools
Quick LookSpace
Get Info⌘I
Open With…⌘Return
Reveal in Finder⇧⌘R
Copy path⌥⌘C
Command palette⌘K

Finder conventions where they exist; chords where they earn their keep. Every key is rebindable — nothing to relearn.
